subject.title: fix: stabilize OpenClaw beta setup and PT-PT formatting

question: Should the Companion retain its setup-proven default until a fixed stable OpenClaw release passes setup E2E, or intentionally ship a package line that currently fails the supported WSL setup path?
rationale: The evidence establishes that 2026.7.1 fails setup and that a beta contains a candidate upstream fix, but only maintainers can choose the supported-release policy and acceptable user-facing outage risk.

options.title: Wait for a proven stable
options.body: Keep or restore the setup-proven stable default, validate the next fixed stable release through fresh-install and upgrade E2E, and then update the LKG.

options.title: Split safe fixes now
options.body: Land the invariant-formatting and independently proven lifecycle work separately while deferring the package pin until official-package setup proof is green.

options.title: Accept the failing default
options.body: Ship 2026.7.1 despite the known first-run setup failure and explicitly own the resulting onboarding outage.

recommendation.title: Wait for a proven stable
recommendation.body: Keep or restore the setup-proven stable default, validate the next fixed stable release through fresh-install and upgrade E2E, and then update the LKG.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged history spans release integration, Gateway behavior, and the prior invariant-formatting change, making them the best available routing candidate for this supported-package decision.
